subject: Dedicated reservation options — cluster footprint, min GPU floor & ramp cadence
messages:
From: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>
To: Marta Ruiz <marta@orionbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-19T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated reservation options for OrionBio (initial options)

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Based on the throughput profile you shared and your team's latency targets, I sketched three reservation paths below. Each is intended to balance predictable capacity with cost efficiency and a clear onramp cadence. Please review and tell me which you'd like to explore in the term sheet.

Option A — Compact Pilot (low-risk)
- Cluster: 8 x A100-equivalent GPUs (single availability zone)
- Min GPU floor: 6 active (warm standby + preemptible burst)
- Ramp: 2-week pilot, then decision point to expand
- Best for: validation workloads and small-volume inference (proof-of-concept)

Option B — Standard Anchor (recommended)
- Cluster: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs (multi-AZ for resilience)
- Min GPU floor: 12 active
- Ramp: 4-week staged ramp (25% -> 50% -> 75% -> 100%) over 10 weeks for traffic smoothing
- Best for: production go‑live with predictable growth and room for batching optimizations

Option C — Growth Slate (high throughput)
- Cluster: 32 x A100-equivalent GPUs (reserved pool + surge lanes)
- Min GPU floor: 24 active
- Ramp: 8–12 week phased activation with warm-up credits and burst windows
- Best for: heavy real‑time inference and embedding backfills

Notes: all options include prefix/KV caching recommendations, automatic batch sizing guidance, and a suggested rollback policy (canary -> full). Attachment: Draft_RSV_Options_OrionBio_v1.pdf (high-level pricing + activation examples).

Next step: if you can confirm which option aligns with procurement appetite, I’ll draft a dealbook and include a concrete ramp schedule + signable slate.

Thanks,
Camila Reyes

Hi Camila —

Appreciate the clear framing. A few clarifying items from my end before we engage procurement formally:

1) For Option B (Standard Anchor) what do you mean operationally by "Min GPU floor: 12 active"? Is that a continuous minimum billed or a warm-standby that we can scale down during off-hours?
2) Can you map the ramp cadence to expected token throughput and expected p99 latency? We need those numbers for the architecture review.
3) Any flexibility on the warm-up credits or a partial prepayment to shorten the ramp? Procurement will ask about credits vs. discounts.

Also looping in our procurement mailbox. We are likely to prefer a staged commitment but want to see the activation milestones.

Thanks,

Subject: Re: Dedicated reservation options for OrionBio (mapping to throughput & credits)

Marta —

Great questions. Below I've expanded Option B with concrete operational guardrails and the expected performance envelope. I've also noted where warm-up credits would apply. I put a small sheet together — link below and attached the SLA question workbook.

Standard Anchor (Option B) — concrete mapping- Cluster: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs, multi-AZ (spread across 2 AZs)
- Commitment billing: monthly for reserved pool; we guarantee baseline availability of the Min GPU floor
- Min GPU floor semantics: 12 GPUs guaranteed (billed as reserved capacity). Additional 4 GPUs are soft burst capacity we will keep warm for short-term traffic spikes — they can be used within the reserved pool but are not guaranteed during extreme failures.
- Expected throughput (avg): ~120k tokens/sec aggregate (model: open-llm-3-medium quantized), estimated 1.5k concurrent short-chat QPS with typical context lengths
- p95/p99 latency (inference only): ~90ms / ~180ms (with continuous batching tuned for your workload), depends on request sizing
- Ramp schedule: week-by-week activation. Example plan:
  * Weeks 1–2: activate 4 GPUs (smoke + perf tuning)
  * Weeks 3–6: step to 8 -> 12 GPUs (validation + partial production)
  * Weeks 7–10: full activation to 16 GPUs and enable burst lanes
- Warm-up credits: we recommend a 400 GPU-hour credit pool applied to the first 6 weeks to accelerate cached KV population and reduce cold-run instability. Credits can be allocated as discount or usage credit per procurement preference.

Trade-offs: the 12-GPU min reduces cold-start risk but carries committed cost. If procurement prefers lower committed spend, Option A (Compact Pilot) reduces floor to 6 GPUs and moves more of the risk into short-term burst pricing.

I've attached OrionBio_MLP_SLA_ask.xlsx with the requested fields filled (billing cadence options and sample DocuSign clauses). Google sheet for activation milestones: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/1OrionReservePlan

Would you like us to draft a signable slate with the Standard Anchor and the 400 GPU-hour warmup credit? If yes, we can include a 10-week staged activation table and turn-around the DocuSign link within 48 hours.

Best,
Camila

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Camila Reyes <camila_reyes@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-07-20T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: margin / buffer considerations for ORION-5621

Camila / Karthik —

Quick internal note on the proposal economics if we push Standard Anchor with 12 GPU min: 
- Buffer: recommend a 10–15% buffer on top of the committed min for the first 8 weeks to account for KV-cache warmup inefficiency and burst from evaluation traffic. We can cover some of this with the warm-up credits but not all.
- Warm-up credit structure: 400 GPU-hours is reasonable; if procurement requests more, suggest converting incremental hours into a time-limited discount instead of a higher committed floor.
- SLA exception: add a 30-day operational review clause at week 6 to assess steady-state and canonicalize committed floor or rebaseline to 10 GPUs if usage is consistently sub-minimum.

I'll be prepared to show a few run-rate scenarios for margin and unit economics if needed in procurement.

—Ben
Head of Deals, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com

Hi Marta / procurement team —

Following internal alignment, here's a concise proposed path that matches what we discussed and what procurement flagged:

Agreed proposal (draft for signature)
- Slate: Standard Anchor (Option B)
- Cluster: 16 x A100-equivalent GPUs, multi-AZ
- Min GPU floor: 12 reserved GPUs (monthly billing)
- Ramp cadence: 10-week staged activation (Weeks 1–2: 4 GPUs smoke; Weeks 3–6: jump to 12; Weeks 7–10: full 16 with burst lanes)
- Warm-up support: 400 GPU-hour credit applied to the first 6 weeks (can be modeled as a usage credit or discount per your procurement preference)
- Review checkpoint: operational review at week 6 with potential rebaseline clause (mutual agreement required to move floor)

Next steps
1) I’ll generate a signable slate with the exact billing table and milestone dates and send via DocuSign.
2) Procurement to confirm warm-up credit preference (credit vs. discount) so we model pricing correctly.
3) Once signed, our onboarding team will schedule a 90-minute tech kickoff and share the activation timeline with your infra leads.
